boundaries.label: CIPMS application (Next.js on Vercel + MongoDB Atlas)
External providers (Meta WABA + TRAI DLT regulated)

cards.title: Core flow — launching a campaign
items: 1. Admin composes campaign in UI: picks audience segment, template, schedule.
2. API persists the campaign; CampaignService validates and launches.
3. DispatchService expands the audience to one send_job per contact.
4. Jobs enter the BullMQ queue (Upstash Redis) with per-channel rate limits.
5. Worker pops a job, checks ConsentService (opt-out + DLT window), then calls the channel adapter.
6. Adapter calls the provider API; provider delivers to Pradhan on WhatsApp or SMS.

cards.title: Three sending modes (same queue)
items: Ad-hoc — send.schedule.mode = "immediate"; jobs enqueued at launch.
Scheduled — send.schedule.mode = "scheduled" + send_at; jobs enqueued when the clock hits.
Selective — audience.mode = "ad_hoc" + contact_ids chosen by admin.
Drip + recurring come later on the same pipeline — no new infrastructure.

cards.title: Compliance gates (non-negotiable)
items: ConsentService checks contact.opt_outs[channel] before every send.
SMS Promotional: window enforced to 10 AM-9 PM IST (TRAI).
WhatsApp: outside 24-hour session window requires an approved template (Meta).
Inbound STOP / Meta opt-out webhook flips opt_outs[channel] permanently.
Every send_job stores the rendered body for audit; message_events keeps raw webhook payloads.

cards.title: Why these pieces
items: contacts is separate from users so campaigns can target voters without login rows.
send_jobs is a flat collection (not embedded) so the queue can scan millions of docs.
Adapters implement a WhatsAppProvider / SmsProvider interface — swap providers without touching services.
AnalyticsService reads send_jobs with the same aggregation pattern as /api/reports/aggregate.
Webhook ingestion is the only path that writes delivered / read / replied statuses — no polling.

cards.title: Phased build (independently useful)
items: Phase 1 — Scaffold models + static audience + composer UI (no sending yet).
Phase 2 — WhatsApp live via AiSensy; ad-hoc + scheduled; webhook + basic analytics.
Phase 3 — SMS via MSG91 (DLT registration); multi-channel fallback.
Phase 4 — Dynamic segments (saved queries over contacts + survey responses).
Phase 5 — Replies inbox + cost dashboard + CSV audit export.
Phase 6 — Drip sequences + recurring campaigns + A/B tests.

cards.title: Open questions to lock before Phase 1
items: Single candidate vs multi-candidate vs multi-tenant.
Who gets messaged first — Pradhans only, or Pradhans + voters from survey responses.
Monthly send budget target — drives provider pricing tier.
Template approval workflow — admin role or super_admin only.
Two-way replies in Phase 2 or deferred to Phase 5.
WhatsApp cost (~Rs 1 / conversation) acceptable, or SMS-first (~Rs 0.20)?
